title: Choose the appropriate visa type for your situation
description: Mexico offers Temporary Resident (1-4 years), Permanent Resident, and tourist visa (180 days). Research which fits your situation.

title: Confirm your consulate jurisdiction
description: Mexican visa applications are based on where you legally reside. Find your assigned consulate.

title: Decide on a target city or region
description: Mexico City, Guadalajara, Mérida, Puerto Vallarta, Oaxaca are popular. Consider climate, cost, and lifestyle.

title: Create a relocation budget
description: Factor in visa fees, flights, initial housing, health insurance, and 3-6 months of living expenses.

title: Understand financial requirements
description: Temporary Resident visa requires proof of income (~$2,500 USD/month) or savings (~$42,000 USD in bank for 12 months).

title: Gather bank statements (12 months)
description: Showing consistent income or sufficient savings. Statements must show your name, account number, and running balance.

title: Get passport photos to Mexican specifications
description: Mexican visa photos have specific requirements - white background, no glasses, specific dimensions.

title: Prepare proof of address
description: Utility bill, bank statement, or lease showing your current residence in your home country.

title: Complete visa application form
description: Download and fill out the application form from the Mexican consulate website.

title: Schedule visa appointment at consulate
description: Book appointment online. Wait times vary by consulate - plan ahead.

title: Submit visa application
description: Attend appointment with all documents. Visa is usually approved same day and ready in 1-2 weeks.

title: Book temporary accommodation
description: Airbnb or short-term rental for first few weeks while you find permanent housing.

title: Enter Mexico and get FMM stamped
description: Your visa sticker allows entry. Immigration will stamp your passport and process your entry.

title: Exchange visa for Resident Card within 30 days
description: Visit INM (Instituto Nacional de Migración) to exchange your visa sticker for a resident card. Must be done within 30 days of arrival.

title: Get CURP (population registry number)
description: Free ID number needed for many services. Can get at INM or RENAPO offices.

title: Get RFC (tax ID) if planning to work/earn
description: Required if you'll have Mexican income. Get at SAT (tax office) with CURP and proof of address.

title: Open Mexican bank account
description: Major banks: BBVA, Santander, Banorte, HSBC. Requires resident card, proof of address, and sometimes RFC.

title: Find long-term housing
description: Search on Inmuebles24, Segundamano, or Facebook groups. Consider furnished vs unfurnished.

title: Set up utilities
description: CFE (electricity), water (varies by city), gas, internet (Telmex, Izzi, Totalplay).

title: Get Mexican phone number
description: Major carriers: Telcel, AT&T, Movistar. Prepaid SIMs are easy and affordable.

title: Research health insurance options
description: Options include IMSS (public), private insurance (GNP, AXA), or international plans. Consider Seguro Popular for basic coverage.

title: Register for IMSS if eligible
description: Public health insurance available to residents. Low cost and covers most needs.
